human_tolerance.notes: The most abundant landbird in North America by the Partners in Flight 2019 estimate, and a familiar lawn bird: it pulls earthworms from short grass and nests on houses, sheds and trees in settled areas.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: One of the first North American birds to lay eggs, with normally two to three broods in a breeding season lasting April to July. A clutch is three to five cyan eggs incubated by the female alone; the eggs hatch after 14 days and the chicks leave the nest a further two weeks later. A new nest is built for each brood, the first in an evergreen tree or shrub in northern areas and later broods in deciduous trees.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: On the winter grounds it assembles in large flocks at night to roost in trees in secluded swamps or dense vegetation, breaking up during the day to feed on fruits and berries in smaller groups. Males defend a breeding territory in summer and are less social then.

vocalizations.description: A complex, almost continuous carol of discrete units, often repeated and spliced together into a string with brief pauses between. Among the earliest birds to sing at dawn, and among the last at dusk; the song period runs from late February or early March to late July or early August, and style varies by time of day and region.
An alarm call, and separately a 'scold' call; Wikipedia's vocalisation section names both and illustrates them in a recording, but does not describe either further.

conservation.note: Wikipedia states IUCN evaluated it as least concern and that the population trend appears stable.

range.note: Breeds from Alaska and northern Canada south over most of the continent and winters across the southern United States to Central America.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Feeds in small groups on the ground and in short grass, walking rather than hopping; it flies to and from feeding sites and glides.

traits.nest_type.note: The nest is built of long coarse grass, twigs, paper and feathers, smeared with mud and cushioned with soft material, in a tree or shrub; Cup chosen for that mud-cup construction.

traits.mass_kg.note: Wikipedia's stated average of 77 g, within a male range of 72-94 g and a female range of 59-91 g.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Wikipedia gives an average lifespan of about two years in the wild and a longest known wild lifespan of 14 years; the typical value used here is the average.

traits.diet.note: Wikipedia gives about 40 percent small invertebrates (mainly insects, including earthworms, beetle grubs, caterpillars and grasshoppers) and 60 percent wild and cultivated fruits and berries, which is the split recorded here; the diet object has no separate berry key, so the berry share is carried as a separate habitat resource instead.

traits.social.note: Wikipedia describes large flocks on the winter grounds, smaller feeding groups by day, and territorial males alone on the breeding territory; Flock with an authored upper bound of 250 is the single-value mapping, and the bound is judgement.

traits.activity_pattern.note: 'The species is active mostly during the day', assembling in flocks at night to roost.

traits.defense.note: Adults are vigilant in feeding flocks and give an alarm call; canids take fledglings from the ground and raccoons prey on nests. Flee is the judgement mapping.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: tolerant of people on lawns and in gardens, but quickly flushes and scolds at a close approach to the nest.

habitat.use.note: The ground share follows the described earthworm-and-fruit ground feeding and short-grass foraging; the arboreal share covers nesting in trees and shrubs and communal roosting.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet; the monthly windows are judgement, tied to insect availability in the breeding season and fruiting later in the year; the nest_platform share covers the use of buildings and ledges for the first brood.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Wikipedia records the species as the most abundant North American landbird (Partners in Flight, 2019) and describes nests on houses and in gardens; the lawn-foraging detail follows its earthworm diet.

seasonal.strategy.note: Wikipedia calls it a migratory bird and describes both breeding and wintering ranges, with large flocks on the winter grounds. winter_fraction is authored judgement: most northern birds migrate, while southern and urban birds are resident year-round.

seasonal.phases.note: Breeding season months April to July, brood number, clutch size, incubation of 14 days and nest-leaving two weeks later are all from the Breeding section; the wintering phase follows the Behaviour section.

seasonal.life_stages.note: The 42-day juvenile duration is the 14-day incubation plus the 14 days to nest-leaving, with the post-fledging period to independence added as judgement; the scale is authored judgement.

vocalizations.note: Song description, its dawn timing and its February-to-August season are from the Vocalization section. The alarm entry records only what Wikipedia supports, that an alarm call and a separate scold call exist; the cooldown is authored judgement.

look.note: Colours from Wikipedia's description of a grey-brown back, blackish head, white eye ring, rusty-orange breast and white belly, with a yellow bill; the palette has no yellow slot, so the bill is drawn from the accent colour. The eye-ring part and proportions are authored judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program. food_tag is 'invertebrate' because 40 percent of the diet is earthworms and insects and foraging is on the ground; flee_m is judgement at the program's default for a bird that flushes readily.
